_README: Each mutation breaks ONE behaviour the fixture claims to cover. Aim them at distinct branches — a mutation that neuters the whole hook only proves the suite notices a corpse. `why` is printed in the run output, so write it as the thing that would be silently broken. A key names the file to mutate, resolved the same way run-fixtures resolves a hook. Add "suite": "<hook>" when the mutated file is a shared library, so the run exercises a suite that actually consumes it.

merge-grant.why: a negated request arms the grant, so "don't merge yet" makes a merge approvable
a clause break stops ending a negation, so "don't close 19 but merge 17" no longer arms
notification text counts as the user's words, so an agent's own "ready to merge" arms the grant
a subagent's hand-back counts as the user's words, so its "open the PR" arms the pr grant
a typographic apostrophe stops normalising, so a typed “don’t merge” arms the grant
a negated PR request arms the pr grant, so "don't open a PR yet" drops the PR prompt
open after keep or leave reads as the verb, so "keep open the PRs from dependabot" arms the pr grant
an interjection stops leading a clause, so "ok, open PRs for both branches" no longer arms the pr grant
a number or `new` counts as a determiner again, so "list the open two PRs that touch auth" arms the pr grant

replace.to: their one two new both another separate

merge-grant.why: the verb window never closes, so a PR mentioned anywhere after "open" arms the pr grant
a comma ends the negation again, so "Don't, please, merge this" arms the grant
only a fixed list negates, so "we shouldn't open a PR yet" arms the pr grant
open mid-clause reads as the verb again, so "list the open draft PRs" arms the pr grant
pull request stops reading as a PR, so "open a pull request against main" arms nothing
a block the strip leaves unbalanced counts as the user's words, so a hand-back quoting its own closing tag arms a grant
a verb directly before PRs arms at once again, so `open PRs?` arms the pr grant
a comma stops ending the verb's reach, so "Leave it open, the PR needs another review" arms the pr grant
a preposition stops ending the verb's reach, so "create a list of PRs older than a week" arms the pr grant

merge-grant.why: a PR number stops naming an existing PR, so "open PR 17 in the browser" arms the pr grant
a clause of interjections stops leading the verb, so "please open PRs for both branches" no longer arms
a comma after an interjection stops leading the verb, so "the build is red, ok, open PRs for both" no longer arms
no stops being an interjection, so "no, open PRs for both" no longer arms

destructive-guard.why: a substitution in a cd stops making the directory unresolvable, so `cd "$(dirname <main>/x)" && git push` reads the session's branch
an escaped space resolves to a missing directory again, so `cd main\ wt && git push` reads the session's branch
a cd behind if/then/do/builtin/command/time stops moving the directory
a case pattern's `)` closes a subshell again, so a later bare push reads the parent directory
every `)` closes a subshell again, so `$((1+1))` pops the directory a cd set
pushd stops moving the directory, so `pushd <main> && git push` reads the session's branch
--git-dir and GIT_DIR= stop naming the repository, so `git --git-dir=<main>/.git push` reads the session's branch
--recurse-submodules stops consuming its value, so `git push --recurse-submodules check origin` reads `check` as the remote
a tags-only push defaults to HEAD again, so `git push origin --tags` from main hard-blocks
an unreadable destination stops standing for the checked-out branch, so `git push origin $(git branch --show-current)` from main passes
a separator glued to a force or delete flag hides it again, so `git push origin x -f;echo` skips the prompt
a colon refspec after the first counts as no delete, so `git push origin x :other` skips the prompt
a subshell's last word inside a case arm reads as a pattern again, so `case x in x) (cd <feature>; true); git push;; esac` keeps the subshell's directory
`esac)` reads as a case pattern again, so a subshell wrapped around a case never closes
an escaped parenthesis counts as a subshell boundary again, so `(cd <main>; echo a\)b; git push)` pops early
the toplevel idiom becomes unresolvable again, so `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git push -u origin HEAD` blocks from a feature checkout
an exported GIT_DIR stops moving the repository, so `export GIT_DIR=<main>/.git && git push` reads the session's branch
a bare GIT_DIR= assignment stops making the repository unknown, so `GIT_DIR=<main>/.git; git push` reads the session's branch
unset GIT_DIR stops restoring the directory's repository, so `export GIT_DIR=<main>/.git; unset GIT_DIR; git push` blocks from a feature checkout
an export with no value stops making the repository unknown, so `export GIT_DIR && git push` reads the session's branch
a push inside a shell string reads the segment's directory again, so `sh -c "cd <main> && git push"` from a feature checkout passes
an abbreviated long option stops naming its option, so `git push --recu check origin` from main reads `check` as the remote
a bundled -o stops taking its value, so `git push -uo ci.skip origin` from main reads `ci.skip` as the remote
a force refspec with `~`, `^` or `@` stops asking, so `git push origin +HEAD~1:feature` rewinds the remote unprompted
pushd -n stops leaving the directory alone, so `cd <main> && pushd -n <feature> && git push` passes
a push that closes its shell string stops counting, so `cd {push_main} && bash -c "git push"` reads no push
an unquoted substitution as the remote stops defaulting to HEAD, so `cd {push_main} && git push $(echo) origin` passes
an abbreviated or bundled delete stops asking, so `git push -qd origin x` and `--del` pass silently
an abbreviated --force-with-lease stops asking, so `git push --force-w origin x` passes silently
cd stops skipping its options, so `cd -P -- {push_main} && git push` reads `--` as the directory
cd with options and no operand stops going home, so `cd -P && git push` reads the session's branch
a push anywhere after git counts again, so `git stash push -m wip` on a main checkout hard-blocks
checkout or switch anywhere after git counts again, so `git -C <main> grep -n checkout` blocks as a branch switch
branch moves stop being recorded, so `git checkout main && git push` from a feature checkout passes
a checkout of a ref with paths counts as a branch move, so `git checkout main README.txt && git push` blocks
a worktree the command adds stops carrying its branch, so a push from a new -b worktree hard-blocks
a directory the command makes falls back to the session branch, so a bare push there reads the session's
a subshell's export leaks again, so `cd <main> && (export GIT_DIR=<feature>/.git); git push` passes
a substitution's export leaks again, so `x=$(export GIT_DIR=<feature>/.git); git push` passes
the toplevel loses the rest of its word, so `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/../push-main && git push` passes
the matching refspec stops counting, so `git push origin :` only asks as a delete
only the first push in a shell string is read again, so `bash -c "git push origin x && git push origin main"` passes
escaped quotes in a shell string stay escaped, so `bash -c "git push origin \"main\""` passes
a glued -o value takes the next word again, so `git push -oo origin main` reads `main` as the remote
GIT_DIR naming a worktree's .git file stops resolving, so `git --git-dir=<main wt>/.git checkout -b x` passes
a cd inside eval stops moving later segments, so `eval "cd <main>" && git push` passes
xargs stops making a bare push name its branch, so `echo main | xargs git push origin` passes
a push refspec set with -c stops counting, so `git -c remote.origin.push=HEAD:refs/heads/main push origin` passes
a parenthesis in a kept shell string pops a subshell again, so `(cd <main>; bash -c 'echo )'; git push)` passes
a case pattern with a space before its parenthesis stops counting, so its arm's cd is lost
a force bundled with -4 stops asking, so `git push -4f origin x` passes silently
a quoted substitution as the remote defaults to HEAD again, so `git push "$(git remote)" x` from main blocks
a word that is literally TOPLEVEL reads as the checkout again, so `cd TOPLEVEL && git push` reads the session's branch

pr-create-guard.why: the stack form stops being recognised, so a stack submit skips every check
the dirty-tree block on a stack submit becomes advisory instead of blocking
the working directory stops being resolved, so every git check reads the session repo
an unresolvable default branch goes back to blocking, asserting a zero diff nobody measured

if ! git "${GITC[@]}" rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/${DEFAULT_BRANCH}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exit 0
fi

pr-create-guard.why: the command stops being stripped, so the guard fires on its own trigger in a -m body
only the FIRST cd is read, so `cd a && cd b` grades the repo the command left

stateful-op-reminder.why: the command stops being stripped, so the reminder fires on its trigger in a -m body

_lib/strip-cmd.why: an executed heredoc is blanked again, hiding a real invocation behind three lines of shell

_lib/split-cmd-segments.pl.why: a completed substitution is discarded, hiding a nested destructive command
a substitution scope opener is omitted, so checkout directory state cannot be restored safely
a substitution cuts its enclosing segment again, so `git -C "$(…)" push` reaches no push check
process substitution stops being a substitution, so `diff <(git push origin main) x` passes
a substitution after `=` is split off its option again, so `git push --push-option=$(echo x) origin` from main reads it as the remote
the toplevel splits from the rest of its word, so `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/../push-main && git push` passes
a redirect inside the toplevel substitution makes it unreadable, so `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"` blocks
a bar inside [[ ]] splits the segment again, so its `)` pops the subshell holding the cd
a substitution glued into an option value splits off the rest, so `-o$(echo x)y origin` reads `y` as the remote

_lib/strip-quoted-args.pl.why: empty quote fragments stop composing executable tokens
exec-wrapped shells lose their executable heredoc bodies
backtick escape decoding corrupts a nested executable token
quoted substitutions are treated as data, hiding nested mutations
an ordinary heredoc loses its executable expansions
quoted heredoc delimiters stop suppressing literal body text
a wrapper hides the shell after it, so `printf a | xargs -I{} sh -c 'git push origin main'` reads the push as data
su -c and flock -c strings stop counting as code, so `su -c 'git push origin main'` reads the push as data
watch's operand stops counting as code, so `watch -n 60 'git push origin main'` reads the push as data
a path beside a quoted substitution is masked again, so `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/." && git push` blocks
macOS and Linux exec wrappers stop being looked through, so `caffeinate -i bash -c 'git push origin main'` passes
